client_brief:
Norvant: explainer motion set

Project overview
Norvant is workflow automation built for finance and operations teams. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Norvant explainer motion set and Norvant press frame set.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); motion_source_metadata.json; source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); norvant_launch_card_2025.pdf; norvant_events.csv; norvant_reception_sign.jpg; norvant_launch_copy.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Norvant explainer motion set: A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- Norvant press frame set: Six genuinely different moments pulled from the delivered cut and brought to one press look with one white point, one black point and one treatment of the window wall, each cut to the ratio its destination needs rather than one frame issued at six sizes. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 1 video file totaling 5.042 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 0 separate audio files. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com motion graphics brief carried in the ledger, in which a client with raw explainer footage, a logo, colour references and a loose outline wants a clear informative cut plus on brand text treatment (lower thirds, call outs, title and end cards) and the linked assets organised so the team can make future tweaks themselves. Co anchored to the same client's stated need for a launch package rather than a single video. REPOSITIONED for connector reality, which is what makes this the honest fuller commission. The headless connector cannot composite type onto a video track, so the on brand text half of the real brief is delivered where it can genuinely be made and edited: press frames pulled from the cut and graded, an announcement canvas set authored as a native editable document, and the eleven city printed cards built as a live merge off the printer's own file. The tightening is done by the shortening route, which chooses its own retained set, and the vertical is a ratio reframe rather than a re shoot. The company is laundered to the coined fictional Norvant, a workflow automation product whose identity is a hexring glyph and a slate and amber wordmark; no real company, product, person or trademark is named, and Freelancer.com is only the sourcing platform.

price_band_and_audience: A one hundred and forty dollar per seat per month B2B product bought by a committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review in the middle of the cycle. The band is load bearing. At this price the buyer is looking for evidence of seriousness, so the kit has to be quiet, specific and legible: a founder who sounds like she knows the domain, press frames that show the actual product, a printed card that looks like it came from a company with a controller, and type that is plain rather than expressive. The same product at a nine dollar self serve band would correctly be launched loud, bright, animated and benefit led, and shipping that here reads as consumer marketing and lengthens the sales cycle because the committee stops believing the numbers. Push the other way into enterprise grey, stock boardrooms and a dense capability matrix and it misprices a product an operations lead adopts in an afternoon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Workflow automation for finance and operations.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. An eleven person company with no in-house designer.
brand_identity.about: Norvant is workflow automation built for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month, and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything we put out has to look like it was made by people who know what they are doing. We are a small team shipping a serious tool, and our March release is the work the whole company has been building toward.
brand_identity.audience: A buying committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review mid-cycle. They are looking for evidence of seriousness and real numbers, and they lengthen the cycle the moment something feels like consumer marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered B2B mid-market. One hundred and forty dollars per seat per month, committee-approved. Not self-serve impulse software, and not heavyweight enterprise. A tool an operations lead can adopt in an afternoon and defend to a controller.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet, credible type system across the cards, the announcement set and the handover: a plain neutral face for detail and body, a measured companion for headings. Nothing expressive, nothing decorative. Legibility at small print sizes matters more than personality.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, confident without selling. States what the product does and lets the facts carry it. No stock smiles, no superlatives. Tells people directly what is and is not true.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files went with the agency that made them. The mark now survives only as the sign on our reception wall: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel. Last year's regional event card exists only as the print-ready file we sent to the printer. We need the mark recovered as scalable artwork and this year's card run rebuilt from last year's file so it matches. No editable logo source, colour build or master template remains on our side.
brand_identity.values: Seriousness you can verify, restraint over noise, and plain honesty about what we could and could not do.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_launch_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's regional event card exactly as it was sent to the printer: a 105 by 148 millimetre card with the event details set as one continuous block and a placed portrait of that city's host.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's card, straight from our printer. We want this year to match it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its details are set as a continuous flow, so the converted layout does not expose one frame per field, and the readout that reports the frame's text back to you omits one run entirely while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past that point is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid on those wrong offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and the missing fields appear nowhere until a card is actually merged and looked at. The file also carries no bleed at all, which cannot be introduced afterward.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_events.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The eleven city event roster: city, venue, street address, date, host name, host title, seat tier line, and a column of per city venue photographs.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The eleven cities. One row each, with the venue picture for that city."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two venue names run long enough that at the card's fixed detail measure the line does not spill or reflow, it simply stops rendering and truncates at the trim edge, which looks like a design choice on a proof. One city appears twice with two different venues because the roster was merged from two spreadsheets, one date is written in a different order from the other ten, and one row's seat tier line is the field the readout drops.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_reception_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld photograph of the reception wall sign: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel under a raking downlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sign on our wall. It is the only place the mark still exists at any size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The glyph is an enclosed ring with a fine internal counter, so background removal returns a solid opaque disc rather than a ring, and a trace that looks clean at full canvas closes that counter at the size the mark actually reproduces on a 105 millimetre card and on an amber ground. The slate cut also runs close to the brushed panel in value across the left third where the downlight falls off, so a selection there takes panel with the ink.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as cleared. The three claims cannot be reworded."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The deliverable relies on absent sound and fails when viewed as supplied.
